title: Retention of Landing Fault Context in the Brake and Steering Control Unit Load

ata.title: Wheels and Brakes — Brake Control Unit

abstract: A control unit software content change that keeps the recorded landing fault context across a power cycle, so that a line engineer can close a post-landing brake message without removing a serviceable wheel and brake assembly.

sections.reason: Twenty-one post-landing brake messages were reported by one operator in eight months, all after landings above thirty-five degrees ambient, all clearing on the next power-up and all leaving a truncated snapshot behind. Two serviceable brake assemblies were removed because the line engineer had nothing to work with. The snapshot introduced by the current software standard is held in volatile memory during the taxi phase and is only committed on a clean shutdown, which is exactly the case that does not happen when the crew power down quickly on a hot turnaround.
sections.description: The proposed software load commits the fault snapshot to non-volatile memory as soon as the triggering event is detected rather than at shutdown, extends the captured window from forty to one hundred and twenty seconds, and adds brake temperature and ambient temperature to the recorded set. The load is LG9P59363BC, which supersedes the standard currently in service. No hardware change is proposed: the switch assembly D3240126111041 already provides the sampling rate needed, which is why the load is conditional on the current software and hardware standard being present. The brake filter position 1GM5 appears in the revised fault tree but is not modified. The change is scoped as software content only. What the unit records is internal to it and the reporting interface to the maintenance system is untouched, so no interface substantiation is expected. Loading is done through the flight deck data loading interface, with the aircraft on the ground and the parking brake set, working in the main gear bay area of zone 721 only for the post-load functional check.
sections.effects: No mass change. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable with the earlier load, because the snapshot record format changes and the maintenance terminal needs the matching reader. Expected effect is the removal of roughly four in five no-fault-found brake assembly removals on hot-turnaround networks, based on the operator data used in the business case. Dispatch relief is unchanged. The brake control unit test task and the associated troubleshooting procedure require reissue, and the maintenance system reader has to be updated at the same time.
sections.embodiment_note: Field loadable, applied at a transit stop in under an hour with the aircraft powered from ground supply. No kit, no long-lead part. The pacing item is the certification credit for the changed recording function rather than any embodiment constraint.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the maintenance terminal reader update travels with this load or needs its own change, and whether aircraft that took the software-only retrofit rather than the hardware and software retrofit are eligible.

type_data.production_impact: Production cut-in at the next scheduled software configuration change

title: Retention of Landing Fault Context in the Brake and Steering Control Unit Load

issue.reason: Reclassified from a software content change to an interface change, with the certification question on retained context added to the open points and the lead time and cost re-estimated against it.
